Testimony in Support of LD 331: "Resolve, Directing the Department of Health and Human Services to Ensure Timely
Reimbursement Under MaineCare Regarding Hospital Cost Reports"
Senator Ingwersen, Representative Meyer, and distinguished members of the Committee on Health and Human Services, my name is Harris Van Pate, and I serve as policy analyst for Maine Policy Institute. Maine Policy is a free market think tank, a nonpartisan, non-profit organization that advocates for individual liberty and economic freedom in Maine. Thank you for the opportunity to provide testimony in support of LD 331, "Resolve, Directing the Department of Health and Human Services to Ensure Timely Reimbursement Under MaineCare Regarding Hospital Cost Reports."
The Need for Timely MaineCare Reimbursement
Hospitals across Maine are essential in providing care to our residents, particularly in rural and underserved communities. However, delayed reimbursements from MaineCare place a significant financial strain on these institutions, limiting their ability to deliver high-quality care, invest in facility improvements, and retain essential healthcare staff. LD 331 addresses this issue by requiring the Department of Health and Human Services (DHHS) to reimburse hospitals at least 75% of the as-filed settlement from cost reports within 90 days of receipt.
Under the current system, hospitals face prolonged delays in receiving reimbursements for already-provided services. These delays create cash flow challenges, making it difficult for hospitals to cover operational costs, purchase medical supplies, and expand services to meet growing patient needs. By ensuring timely reimbursement, LD 331 will help stabilize Maine's hospital network, and support continued patient access to care.
Economic and Operational Benefits
- Financial Stability for Hospitals--Many Maine hospitals, mainly smaller and rural ones, operate on narrow financial margins. Delayed reimbursements create unnecessary financial uncertainty, potentially leading to service reductions or staff layoffs. By guaranteeing at least 75% reimbursement within 90 days, LD 331 provides a much-needed financial cushion, allowing hospitals to plan and allocate resources effectively.
- Improved Patient Care--Ensuring hospitals receive timely payments means they can focus on their core mission--delivering high-quality patient care. Hospitals struggling financially often leads to longer wait times, reduced service availability, and difficulty retaining skilled healthcare professionals. This

legislation will help mitigate these challenges by providing hospitals with more predictable revenue streams. - Preventing Cost Shifting - When hospitals face funding shortfalls due to delayed MaineCare payments, they often compensate by shifting costs to commercially insured patients, increasing healthcare costs for businesses and individuals. Timely reimbursement under LD 331 will help curb this practice, leading to more equitable healthcare pricing across the system. - Alignment with Fiscal Responsibility--LD 331 mandates DHHS implement these reimbursement changes within existing resources. This ensures that necessary reforms are made without increasing the financial burden on taxpayers. The department can fulfill its obligation to hospitals by streamlining administrative processes while maintaining fiscal discipline.
Conclusion
LD 331 is a common-sense solution that supports Maine hospitals, protects patient access to care, and promotes responsible fiscal management. By ensuring that hospitals receive at least 75% of their as-filed cost report settlements within 90 days, we can strengthen our healthcare infrastructure and safeguard services for Maine families.
For these reasons, we respectfully urge the committee to support LD 331. Thank you for your time and consideration.

Re: LD 331 - Resolve, Directing the Department of Health and Human Services to Ensure Timely Reimbursement Under MaineCare Regarding Hospital Cost Reports
Senator Ingwersen, Representative Meyer and members of the Joint Standing Committee on Health and Human Services, thank you for the opportunity to provide information in opposition of LD 331, Resolve, Directing the Department of Health and Human Services to Ensure Timely Reimbursement Under MaineCare Regarding Hospital Cost Reports.
This bill requires the Department of Health and Human Services to amend its rules in Chapter 101: MaineCare Benefits Manual, Chapter III, Section 45, Hospital Services, to require the Department to reimburse at least 75% of the as-filed settlement pursuant to a hospital's cost reports within 90 days of receipt. It requires the Department to accomplish this within existing resources.
The Department is not opposed to the concept of the bill; however, the operationalization of the proposed reimbursement practices is not feasible utilizing existing resources. As written, the Department would be required to borrow funds from future fiscal years in order to make as-filed payments within 90 days of receipt. One-time funding would need to be allocated July 1, 2026, in order to get ahead of the payments and eliminate the need to borrow funding from future fiscal years. If this funding were to be allocated, the Department would have no identified concerns with reimbursing at least 75% of the as-filed settlement pursuant to a hospital's cost reports within 90 days of receipt as proposed in this bill.
The Department would be happy to provide additional information and further discuss the challenges associated with LD 331 and our opposition to moving forward with the bill without allocating one-time funding to support the change. Please feel free to contact me if you have any questions during your deliberation of this bill.
Sincerely,

Michelle Probert Director Office of MaineCare Services Maine Department of Health and Human Services

Testimony of Sarah Calder, MaineHealth
In Support of LD 331, "Resolve, Directing the Department of Health and Human Services to Ensure Timely Reimbursement Under MaineCare
Regarding Hospital Cost Reports"
March 13, 2025
Senator Ingwersen, Representative Meyer and distinguished members of the Joint Standing
Committee on Health and Human Services, I am Sarah Calder, Senior Govemment Afiairs
Director at MaineHealth, and I am here to testify in support of LD 331, "Resolve, Directing the
Department of Health and Human Services to Ensure Timely Reimbursement Under MaineCare
Regarding Hospital Cost Reports."
MaineHealth is an integrated non-profit health care system that provides a continuum of health
care services to communities throughout Maine and New Hampshire. Every day, our over 24,000
care team members support our vision of "Working Together so Our Communities are the Healthiest in America" by providing a range of services from primary and specialty physician services to a continuum of behavioral health care services, community and tertiary hospital care, home health care and a lab.
The legislation before you today directs the Department of Health and_Human Services to
reimburse at least 75% of a hospital's cost report within 90 days, which is the same
reimbursement requirement in place for nursing facilities. Unlike nursing homes, hospitals do not
receive interim settlements until 12 months - or 1 year -- after submission of our cost reports.
As of February 28, we had not received any settlements from MaineCare for our Fiscal Year
2023 (care provided between October 1, 2022 and September 30, 2023) cost reports. This
amount totals nearly $40 million. We are still waiting on reimbursement more than one year after
submitting our cost reports. It is important to note that this is care that has already been provided and the expenses have already been incurred -- in some cases more than 2 years ago -- and we're
still waiting on reimbursement. We also recently submitted our FY 2024 cost reports, for which combined settlements total nearly $61 million. We are currently owed over $100 million by
MaineCare.
These are exceptionally challenging times in health care with many hospitals throughout the state
having less than 30 days cash on hand. LD 331 would help to address cash flow issues by
providing timely payment of care that again, and very importantly, has already been provided.
Thank you for your consideration and I would be happy to answer any questions that you may
'
have.
